BERT4Rec predicts from an appended MASK using bidirectional context and learned positions ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690)). Recommended independent fixtures: construct expected tokens/indices manually, without importing production preprocessing/readout helpers. For width six, history [a,b] must produce [0,0,0,a,b,MASK], reading index 5; count_nonzero−1 incorrectly selects index 2. Inject distinct position-coded hidden states to expose wrong gathering, and inspect actual encoder inputs to detect omitted MASK. Include singleton, partially padded and full-capacity histories; the latter must truncate before appending. Training/export agreement alone cannot establish correctness.

For attention padding exclusion, perturb only masked padding embeddings through a test hook, retaining identical token masks, real-token positions and weights: real-position outputs should remain unchanged. Force nonzero padding representations so disabling exclusion measurably changes the result. Do not assume invariance after adding left padding: absolute positions can shift ([original implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/modeling.py)). Separately force PAD/MASK logits highest and verify neither becomes a recommendation. Test all four category routes with distinct synthetic checkpoint fingerprints, overlapping local item IDs and independently specified expected outputs; reorder and interleave requests to expose routing/cache errors. These fixtures require no additional trained models.

Count a mutant as exercised only when instrumentation confirms its changed path ran and the fixture makes its effect observable; count a kill only when the intended semantic assertion fails. Report killed, surviving, unexercised and invalid/equivalent mutants separately ([mutation states](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/mutation-testing-elements/mutant-states-and-metrics/)). Clean controls must pass unchanged models and benign request permutations. Proposed tolerances: exact token/index/route checks; deterministic eval-mode FP32 scores atol=1e−6, rtol=1e−5, calibrated against repeat-run noise. Require deliberate mutant effects comfortably above tolerance; compare ranks only with score margins exceeding numerical uncertainty.
